PERSISTENT DEMANDS ARE AN OFFENCE, NOT A PROOF OF LOVE.
⚠️ UNDER 18? THINK BEFORE YOU SEND.
A “private” photo is not always private once it enters the digital world.
For minors, requesting, creating, possessing, storing or forwarding sexually explicit material can have serious legal consequences. Section 67B of the Information Technology Act, 2000 specifically addresses electronic material depicting children in sexually explicit acts or conduct.
As a law student, I believe cyber-law awareness should begin before the mistake happens, not after the police complaint, seizure of devices, or criminal proceedings.
📌 Remember: • Consent does not make unlawful child sexual material legal.
• Forwarding is not “just sharing.”
• Screenshots and digital files can become evidence.
• Deleting a message does not necessarily erase the digital trail.
• What looks like a joke online can have consequences offline.

The safest rule is simple:
DON’T REQUEST IT.
DON’T CREATE IT.
DON’T SAVE IT.
DON’T FORWARD IT.

🔐 Think before you click. Think before you send.
